topic: The reciprocity rule: why favors and free samples work
title: The Reciprocity Rule: Why Favors Create Debts
voiceover: Does getting a small favor make us want to give something back? In one experiment, people who got a favor bought more raffle tickets than those who did not. In 1971, Dennis Regan ran an experiment in which people rated paintings. During a break, a partner of the researcher, Joe, sometimes returned with a Coke for the participant. Later, Joe asked participants to buy raffle tickets. This held even when they said they didn't like Joe. Regan linked the result to a norm of reciprocity: we feel we should repay. It was one laboratory experiment. Applying it to free samples in stores is an extension, not something this study tested. So a small favor may create a pull to repay, even toward someone you don't like. Tomorrow: why do we judge other people's character but explain away our own behavior?
